niche.title: You Eat a Rainbow, but Your Poop Stays Brown
niche.description:
Green salad, red tomatoes, white rice: whatever colour goes in, healthy poop comes out brown. Here is where that brown really comes from.

Digestion breaks down most food pigments. The brown is a pigment called stercobilin, made by gut bacteria from bilirubin, a yellow pigment the liver sends into the gut with bile. When bile ducts are blocked, stool turns pale or clay-coloured.

Bilirubin comes mainly from haem in old red blood cells. Cleanup cells called macrophages, mostly in the spleen and liver, remove an estimated two to three million worn-out red cells every second and break them down.
